result.title: Counting Contributions, Not Views: Occlusion-Aware Densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting
result.comment: Accepted at ACCV 2026 (Oral). Includes the supplementary material as appendix. Code: https://github.com/MarcelRogge/occlusion-aware-3dgs
result.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting grows a dense scene from a sparse initialization through adaptive density control (ADC), driven by per-Gaussian statistics gathered during rendering. These statistics pass a frustum-based visibility filter blind to occlusion: fully occluded Gaussians still count as observed, diluting the averaged gradient signal and suppressing densification precisely where geometry is occluded. We correct this with an occlusion-aware filter that restricts densification statistics to views in which a Gaussian actually contributes, and replace the criterion's raw view-count normalizer with an average-contribution one. Integrated into a StopThePop-based framework, the two together improve every image-quality metric over the occlusion-blind baseline on occlusion-heavy scenes (up to 6% lower LPIPS), at less than half the Gaussians a view-count normalizer requires. Under the longer schedules these large scenes require, the count stays bounded where most criteria diverge, and on smaller benchmarks our method stays competitive at a fraction of the competitors' count.

AI.brief_summary: 该文改进 3D Gaussian Splatting 的自适应密度控制，用遮挡感知过滤把致密化统计限制在 Gaussian 真正产生贡献的视角上，并以平均贡献归一化替代原始视角计数，从而在遮挡密集场景减少冗余点数并提升图像质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按实际贡献而非视锥可见计数」的重加权思路，可能可供核查 latent 推理中视觉证据是否真正被使用、以及状态贡献分配与冗余归因的评价方式；但与 VLM 推理无直接联系，属较远的类比线索。
